Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement and technical due diligence, Metronix needs the completed SIG questionnaire and a small set of supporting artifacts to progress to the legal review. On the questionnaire we've flagged controls around:
- KMS / key management provenance and split custody
- Runtime telemetry and retention
- Data-in-transit and at-rest encryption details
- SOC 2 scope & report availability (if you have an attestation)

Could you confirm what you can deliver by next Tuesday (2027-05-11)? Ideally we need a control mapping (SIG->Redwood controls), a sample kms proof PDF, and a short telemetry sample that shows retention and anonymization behavior.

If there are any items requiring NDAs or redaction, let us know. Happy to set a quick 20-min call if it's easier.

Best,
Jane

Please confirm retention policy language you referenced "default 30 days, configurable with enterprise contract" — we need explicit confirmation for the redaction statement.
2) KMS: does Redwood support split custody/HSM-backed keys where Metronix retains the signing key and Redwood holds an encrypted wrapping key? If so, please point to the architecture diagram section or provide a one-paragraph confirmation for our crypto lead.

If those two items are answered, we can advance to Legal and Procurement.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire and initial evidence asks — answers and closure

Oliver / Jane — thanks for the review and the clear asks. Short answers and links below: 

1) Telemetry retention and PII: By default, request/response traces are retained 30 days. Customers on enterprise contracts can configure retention windows (7–90 days) and elect to enable prompt redaction at ingestion. The runtime-telemetry-sample.txt and the attached readme outline the anonymization steps we apply (hashing, redaction rules for email/credit-card patterns, and token-level masking).

2) KMS split custody: Redwood supports HSM-backed key wrapping and customer-controlled key material via our Bring-Your-Own-Key option. In a split-custody flow Metronix can hold the signing key in its HSM; Redwood stores only an encrypted wrapping key and performs operations under customer policy. See architecture-diagram-redwood-2027.png (legend section) and the kms-key-provenance-sample.pdf for an example of the metadata fields captured during issuance. If you would like a formal attestation letter, we will route that request to Legal and the Trust team — please confirm the exact wording you need.

Drive folder with artifacts and short narratives: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqRedwood-Metronix-SIG
HubSpot record for the opportunity: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/MTX-9987

Next steps: Jane / Procurement — if the answers above are sufficient, please confirm and we'll issue the final packet (PDF bundle) and circulate a brief attestation template for Legal to review.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Vivek Kulkarni
